whatItIs.text: The sweet Genovese basil of the West is one herb of a vast family — the clove-like scent comes from eugenol, and Thai, lemon, and holy basil are distinct cousins.

historyNote.text: Basil is native to tropical and subtropical Asia, from India and Sri Lanka across to southern China and down to northern Australia; the genus Ocimum includes at least 60 varieties that cross-pollinate freely.

howToChoose.text: Choose bunches with perky, unblemished leaves and no blackening; avoid flowering stems for cooking (the leaves turn bitter).

storage.text: Keep like cut flowers — stems in water, loosely bagged, away from the coldest shelf, which blackens basil.

useItUp.text: Wilted basil still makes great pesto or basil oil; blitz with olive oil and freeze in cubes, or layer the good leaves with tomato and cheese for a caprese finish.

substitutions.note: anise edge; holds up better to heat

substitutions.substitute: baby spinach + a little dried basil
substitutions.note: in pesto when fresh basil is short
